functions.signature: void bwapi_abi_version(int32_t* major, int32_t* minor, int32_t* patch)
functions.doc: The ABI's own version, written to the three out-params; any of them may be NULL and is then skipped. 0.x is explicitly unstable; append-only begins at 1.0, the exit of the consumers phase. Three int32_t out-params rather than a packed word, so there is nothing to document about packing.
The ABI's own version as "major.minor.patch".
BWAPI::CLIENT_VERSION of the pinned BWAPI (10003 today). The server refuses a client whose version differs from its own, so a host can check compatibility before connecting.
SVN_REV of the pinned BWAPI, from upstream's own revision generator (plan section 10.3).
1 when the pinned BWAPI was built with BUILD_DEBUG, 0 otherwise.

The BWAPI_ERR_* code latched by the first failing call since the last bwapi_clear_last_error(), or BWAPI_ERR_NONE. Sticky: successful calls do not touch it and reading does not clear it. Clear it at the top of the frame and check it before bwapi_client_update(). This is a different lifetime from BWAPI's own Game::getLastError(), which is per call and comes back through bwapi_game_get_last_error().
The message that came with the latched code: a BWEM::Exception's what(), the two unit ids of an overlap, the name of the export a bad handle was passed to. Empty when nothing is latched.
Resets the sticky error channel to BWAPI_ERR_NONE and clears its message.

Installs where the ABI's own diagnostics go, at BWAPI_LOG_* levels, with the user pointer handed back on every call. NULL disables. Client::connect() still writes to std::cout and std::cerr itself in this version.

Installs a callback invoked at the moment an error is latched, with the code, its message and the user pointer, so a wrapper can raise at the failing call rather than poll. Off by default; NULL disables. The sticky latch is unchanged either way. The callback runs with the re-entrancy depth raised, so a mutating call from inside it is rejected with BWAPI_ERR_REENTRANT_MUTATION once that guard is emitted.

Connects to a running BWAPI server over its shared memory and pipe. Returns 1 on success and 0 when no server is up, in which case retry after a pause. Records the calling thread as the thread every later call must come from. Already connected: latches BWAPI_ERR_ALREADY_CONNECTED and returns 0.

Ends the frame and BLOCKS on the pipe until the server hands back the next one. Every event index and snapshot from the previous frame is invalid afterwards. If the server has gone away, bwapi_client_is_connected() is 0 on return.
Tears down BWEM first, because its map points into the game data, then the client. Safe to call when not connected.
1 while connected. Becomes 0 when the server goes away during bwapi_client_update().
The player's id, which is the handle itself: 0..11, the slot in the game's player table.

How many completed units of the type the player has; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type.

How many units of the type the player has killed; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type.

functions.signature: int32_t bwapi_unittype_upgrades(int32_t unit_type, int32_t* out, int32_t cap)
functions.doc: Retrieves the set of upgrades that the unit type can use to enhance its fighting ability. The ids come back ascending, up to cap; returns the total.
Retrieves the upgrade type used to increase the armor of the unit type. For each upgrade, the unit type gains +1 additional armor.
Retrieves the default maximum amount of hit points that the unit type can have.
Retrieves the default maximum amount of shield points that the unit type can have.
Retrieves the maximum amount of energy the unit type can have by default.
Retrieves the default amount of armor that the unit type starts with, excluding upgrades.
Retrieves the default mineral price of purchasing the unit.
Retrieves the default vespene gas price of purchasing the unit.
Retrieves the default time, in frames, needed to train, morph, or build the unit.
Retrieves the amount of supply that the unit type will use when created. It will use the supply pool that is appropriate for its Race.
Retrieves the amount of supply that the unit type produces for its appropriate Race's supply pool.
Retrieves the amount of space required by the unit type to fit inside a Bunker or Transport.
Retrieves the amount of space provided by this Bunker or Transport for unit transportation.
Retrieves the amount of score points awarded for constructing the unit type. This value is used for calculating scores in the post-game score screen.
Retrieves the amount of score points awarded for killing the unit type. This value is used for calculating scores in the post-game score screen.
Retrieves the UnitSizeType of the unit type, which is used in calculations along with weapon damage types to determine the amount of damage that will be dealt to the type.
Retrieves the width of the unit type, in tiles. Used for determining the tile size of structures.
Retrieves the height of the unit type, in tiles. Used for determining the tile size of structures.
Retrieves the tile size of the unit type. Used for determining the tile size of structures.
Retrieves the distance from the center of the unit type to its left edge.
Retrieves the distance from the center of the unit type to its top edge.
Retrieves the distance from the center of the unit type to its right edge.
Retrieves the distance from the center of the unit type to its bottom edge.
A macro for retrieving the width of the unit type, which is calculated using dimensionLeft + dimensionRight + 1.
A macro for retrieving the height of the unit type, which is calculated using dimensionUp + dimensionDown + 1.
Retrieves the range at which the unit type will start targeting enemy units.
Retrieves the sight range of the unit type.
Retrieves the unit type's weapon type used when attacking targets on the ground.

Retrieves the maximum number of hits the unit type can deal to a ground target using its ground weapon. This value is multiplied by the ground weapon's damage to calculate the unit type's damage potential.
Retrieves the unit type's weapon type used when attacking targets in the air.
Retrieves the maximum number of hits the unit type can deal to a flying target using its air weapon. This value is multiplied by the air weapon's damage to calculate the unit type's damage potential.
Retrieves the unit type's top movement speed with no upgrades.
Retrieves the unit's acceleration amount.
Retrieves the unit's halting distance. This is the distance from the unit's destination at which point the unit starts decelerating.
Retrieves a unit's turning rate. This determines how far a unit can rotate in one frame.

Determines if a unit can train other units. For example, UnitTypes::Terran_Barracks.canProduce() will return true, while UnitTypes::Terran_Marine.canProduce() will return false. This is also true for two non-structures: Carrier (can produce interceptors) and Reaver (can produce scarabs).
Checks if the unit type is capable of attacking.
Checks if the unit type is capable of movement.
Checks if the unit type is a flying unit. Flying units ignore ground pathing and collisions.
Checks if the unit type can regenerate hit points. This generally applies to Zerg units.
Checks if the unit type has the capacity to store energy and use it for special abilities.
Checks if the unit type is permanently cloaked. This means the unit type is always cloaked and requires a detector in order to see it.
Checks if the unit type is invincible by default. Invincible units cannot take damage.
Checks if the unit type is an organic unit. The organic property is required for some abilities such as Heal.
Checks if the unit type is mechanical. The mechanical property is required for some actions such as Repair.
Checks if the unit type is robotic. The robotic property is applied to robotic units such as the Probe which prevents them from taking damage from Irradiate.
Checks if the unit type is capable of detecting units that are cloaked or burrowed.
Checks if the unit type is capable of storing resources such as minerals. Resources are harvested from resource containers.

Checks if the unit type is a resource depot. Resource depots must be placed a certain distance from resources. Resource depots are typically the main building for any particular race. Workers will return resources to the nearest resource depot.
Checks if the unit type is a refinery. A refinery is a structure that is placed on top of a geyser . Refinery types are refinery , extractor , and assimilator.
Checks if the unit type is a worker unit. Worker units can harvest resources and build structures. Worker unit types include the SCV , probe, and drone.
Checks if this structure is powered by a psi field. Structures powered by psi can only be placed near a Pylon. If the Pylon is destroyed, then the unit type will lose power.
Checks if this structure must be placed on Zerg creep.
Checks if the unit type spawns two units when being hatched from an Egg. This is only applicable to Zerglings and Scourges.
Checks if the unit type has the capability to use the Burrow technology when it is researched.
Checks if the unit type has the capability to use a cloaking ability when it is researched. This applies only to Wraiths and Ghosts, and does not include units which are permanently cloaked.
Checks if the unit type is a structure. This includes Mineral_Fields and Vespene_Geysers.
Checks if the unit type is an add-on. Add-ons are attachments used by some Terran structures such as the Comsat_Station.
Checks if this structure has the capability to use the lift-off command.
Checks if the unit type is a neutral type, such as critters and resources.
Checks if the unit type is a hero. Heroes are types that the player cannot obtain normally, and are identified by the white border around their icon when selected with a group.
Checks if the unit type is a powerup. Powerups can be picked up and carried by workers. They are usually only seen in campaign maps and Capture_the_flag.
Checks if the unit type is a beacon. Each race has exactly one beacon each. They are UnitTypes::Special_Zerg_Beacon, UnitTypes::Special_Terran_Beacon, and UnitTypes::Special_Protoss_Beacon.

Checks if the unit type is a flag beacon. Each race has exactly one flag beacon each. They are UnitTypes::Special_Zerg_Flag_Beacon, UnitTypes::Special_Terran_Flag_Beacon, and UnitTypes::Special_Protoss_Flag_Beacon. Flag beacons spawn a Flag after some ARBITRARY I FORGOT AMOUNT OF FRAMES.
Checks if this structure is special and cannot be obtained normally within the game.

Identifies if the unit type is used to complement some abilities. These include UnitTypes::Spell_Dark_Swarm, UnitTypes::Spell_Disruption_Web, and UnitTypes::Spell_Scanner_Sweep, which correspond to TechTypes::Dark_Swarm, TechTypes::Disruption_Web, and TechTypes::Scanner_Sweep respectively.
Checks if this structure type produces creep. That is, the unit type spreads creep over a wide area so that Zerg structures can be placed on it.
Checks if the unit type produces larva. This is essentially used to check if the unit type is a Hatchery, Lair, or Hive.

Checks if the unit type is a mineral field and contains a resource amount. This indicates that the unit type is either UnitTypes::Resource_Mineral_Field, UnitTypes::Resource_Mineral_Field_Type_2, or UnitTypes::Resource_Mineral_Field_Type_3.
Checks if the unit type is a neutral critter.
Checks if the unit type is capable of constructing an add-on. An add-on is an extension or attachment for Terran structures, specifically the Command_Center, Factory, Starport, and Science_Facility.

constants.doc: The ABI's own error codes, latched by the sticky first-error channel. A code says which section-4 rule fired. None of these values is ever reused.

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_NONE
values.doc: nothing latched since the last clear

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_WRONG_THREAD
values.doc: a call from a thread other than the update thread

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_REENTRANT_MUTATION
values.doc: a mutating call from inside a callback

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_BWEM
values.doc: a BWEM::Exception, or a map BWEM would crash on

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_INVALID_HANDLE
values.doc: an id that could never have been valid

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_NOT_CONNECTED
values.doc: a game or unit call before connect, or after disconnect

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_BAD_BUFFER
